chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sayyari from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani from Hanan ibn Sadir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who dips his head in water (for cooling), so he said: 'There is no harm, but he should not submerge his head completely. And the woman does not dip her head in water because she retains water in her private part.'
The Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: And deliberate vomiting breaks the fast of the fasting person, and if forced vomiting occurred, there is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.يَسْتَنْقِعُ: to dip the head in water for cooling

ai.seo_question: Does dipping the head in water break the fast, and what is the difference between deliberate and involuntary vomiting?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of cooling oneself while fasting, distinguishing between permissible head-dipping and prohibited full submersion to avoid swallowing water, while offering a specific physiological rationale for women regarding water retention in the private area. The hadith further establishes the principle that deliberate vomiting breaks the fast, whereas involuntary vomiting does not, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on intentionality (*ikhtiyar*) in invalidating acts. This ruling is foundational in the chapter on medical treatments for the fasting, illustrating the practical application of *fiqh al-jism* (jurisprudence of the body) in daily worship.
